notes:
Summary: Mid-market SaaS company (B2B workflow automation). Initially validated core features on hosted API (embeddings + chat assistant). Moving to Dedicated POC to meet latency and compliance needs.

Key technical requirements (paraphrased from calls):
- Workloads: conversational support agent (multi-turn chat), knowledge search (embeddings + reranking), on-demand summarization for long tickets.
- Latency targets: chat p95 <= 250ms for short prompts (under 512 tokens typical), p99 under 600ms. Search/rerank throughput target: 150–250 QPS during peak.
- Cost sensitivity: want clear guidance on unit economics; target blended model cost < $0.15 per 1k requests (POC target).
- Model preferences: prefer open models; willing to accept a quantized 4-bit variant for cost-sensitive routes. Need model-variant catalog and perf/quality tradeoffs from Redwood.
- Routing & availability: require canary + fallback routing plan during rollout. Must support region failover (us-east -> us-west, eu region for EEA customers). Automatic rollback trigger needed for error-rate or latency regressions.

POC Acceptance Criteria (explicit):
1) Canary runs for 48h with 10% of traffic: no more than 0.5% increase in error rate vs hosted baseline and latency p95 within +50ms.
2) Demonstrate routing rules: route by tenant tier -> model variant, and region failover tested under simulated AZ outage.
3) Cost report: expected monthly unit costs and savings options (batching, caching, quantization).
4) Security: SAML SSO working in staging, audit logs surfaced to their SIEM (Splunk).

Canary + Fallback Plan (high-level from SE session):
- Phase 0: baseline run on Redwood Hosted (replica) to capture baseline metrics.
- Phase 1 (Canary): spin Dedicated cluster (reserved pool) with 2 nodes; route 10% traffic for 48h. Monitor latency p95/p99, error rate, token spend.
- Phase 2 (Scale): increase to 40% over 24h if Canary stable.
- Fallback routing: on threshold breach (error rate > 1% sustained 5m OR p95 > baseline + 200ms), traffic automatically reroutes to: 1) quantized model variant in same cluster, 2) if still failing or capacity exhausted -> region failover to sibling region, 3) final fallback -> Redwood Hosted API fallback route.
- Rollback: automated policy to revert model version and routing weights; manual rollback button in Console for immediate revert.
- Observability: token-level cost, per-route latency, and example request traces exported to their tracing endpoint.
